#### 1. Unpublished feature branches are skipped before PR creation

- Finding ID or Review reference: `P1 — Unpublished feature branches are skipped before the PR-open path can publish them`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`) — generated and source-verified.
- Simple description: The PR-open setup requires a tracking ref for the current branch before it reaches the automatic push helper. A new untracked feature branch is skipped instead of being published.
- Example: A developer creates a local feature branch from a tracked base but has not pushed it. `@{u}` is missing, so setup records `UPSTREAM_MISSING` and does not open the PR.
- Why ignored: The observation is technically supported, but its only demonstrated remedy would choose a publication remote or establish tracking for a branch with no existing upstream. That is not an existing control and is excluded by the first-time-publication/alternate-remote Out Of Scope restriction. The complete finding was removed at negative scope and received no later authorization or materiality promotion.

### Accepted

#### 1. Explicit `decisionScript` paths use the server repository instead of the worked repository

- Finding ID: `Reconciliation finding 1`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da`) — generated and verified.
- Simple description: An explicit Python decision-script path is resolved from the server repository, unlike the implicit form. A flow can therefore reject its own checked-in script or run a same-named script from the wrong repository.
- Example: A worked repository supplies `scripts/decision.py` through an explicit `decisionScript` field. The runtime searches the server root instead, so it fails when that server copy is absent or executes the server copy when it exists.
- Why accepted: The reviewed HEAD passed `codeInfo2RootForRun()` as the explicit script root, while the Acceptance Criteria require the checked-in entrypoint to be resolved from the worked repository root. Removing that override uses the existing execution seam, avoids every Out Of Scope restriction and new policy, and materially prevents a wrong script-backed workflow decision. Normal repair `17870939924c22e5981b93a4866cbf0178bcb0c9` removed the override and passed focused worked-repository proof. This resolves this batch's finding, but reverses batch `0000060-rw-20260916T043001Z-2c2cc37d` R1; the unresolved compatibility conflict is not evidence of a fully settled cycle.

#### 2. Python decision scripts continue after a flow is stopped

- Finding ID: `Reconciliation finding 2`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da`) — generated and verified.
- Simple description: The direct Python decision runner does not receive the flow’s cancellation signal. A stopped flow can leave the child script running and can still process its answer.
- Example: A user stops a flow while a Python break decision is running. The child returns `yes`, `runBreakStep` receives `ok`, and the flow can handle that decision before a later cancellation boundary.
- Why accepted: The reviewed HEAD had no script inflight registration, abort listener, or post-await cancellation check, despite the existing flow-stop pattern. Restoring that existing lifecycle behavior is authorized and materially prevents post-stop process and checkpoint/branch authority without adding a new timeout, retry, schema option, or user-facing policy. Normal repair `17870939924c22e5981b93a4866cbf0178bcb0c9` wired that lifecycle and passed deterministic stopped-flow proof within the 62/62 focused run. The advisory stronger-attempt prediction was superseded by normal repair; stronger repair did not run and this finding is not open work.

### Accepted

#### 1. Feature commits can be pushed directly to the tracked base branch

- Finding ID: `F-001`
- Target: `current_repository`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`) — generated and independently verified.
- Simple description: A feature branch tracking the base branch can be pushed straight to that base before the GitHub review flow creates its pull request. That bypasses the review boundary the flow is supposed to provide.
- Example: A feature branch tracks `origin/main`, the story base is `main`, and it has unpushed commits. The flow runs `git push origin HEAD:main`; on a writable unprotected remote, those commits reach `main` before PR creation.
- Why accepted: The reviewed HEAD constructed that command without comparing the current, upstream, and base branch values. The current contract authorizes a current-branch PR and truthful failure handling, while the existing push-result and warning lifecycle can express a pre-command refusal only for this incompatible `HEAD:base` case. The concrete permitted-fast-forward scenario has meaningful impact, and the narrow adapter guard respects every Out Of Scope restriction. Normal repair `49c919a2a02652f9ecf65e67bdfc84146ae6e96f` added that guard and passed 23/23 adapter tests. It remains fixed at current HEAD, and the next two batches reviewed that HEAD. No open implementation task is needed for F-001.

### Accepted

#### 1. Canonical PR metadata and author identity are required before the review lifecycle

- Finding ID: `P2 — Require canonical metadata, including author identity, before a created PR enters the review cycle`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`) — generated the canonical-lookup observation.
  - Copilot: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash (provider default) [current_repository] (`copilot_review`, job `copilot-external-openrouter-deepseek-deepseek-v4-1-flash-80207ac38ad5:current_repository:copilot_review`) — corroborated the missing-author false-clean consequence.
- Simple description: After creating a PR, a failed canonical lookup can currently be represented as a successful PR with synthesized metadata. A PR without an author identity can also make fetched feedback look empty rather than identifying feedback from other users.
- Example: GitHub creates a PR and returns its URL, but the follow-up lookup fails or lacks an author login. The flow can store that PR and continue into its review lifecycle, or return no feedback, even though it cannot distinguish the PR author's material from reviewer feedback.
- Why accepted: Current Acceptance Criteria require an explicit canonical lookup, other-user feedback classification, and truthful warning handling when the GitHub review path cannot proceed. Current HEAD has an existing non-`ok` result plus plan-note/warning/skip seam, making a narrow correction realistic and materially valuable. The accepted core excludes any new retry policy.

#### 2. Scoped Codex detection updates must not leak into the global fallback

- Finding ID: `Medium — Scoped Codex detection updates leak into the process-global fallback`
- Review harnesses:
  - open_code_review [current_repository] (`open_code_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:open_code_review`) — generated the validated source finding.
- Simple description: A Codex detection update inside a test override scope also changes the process-global fallback. An unrelated test can then observe provider state that belonged only to the first test's scope.
- Example: One parallel test sets Codex availability in its AsyncLocalStorage override. A later unscoped consumer reads the module fallback and receives that scoped value, producing order-dependent provider behavior.
- Why accepted: The current story expressly requires parallel and stress reliability without cross-test provider interference. Current HEAD already separates scoped storage from the explicit global helper, so keeping active-scope updates scoped is an authorized, proportionate test-only repair.

### Accepted

#### 1. First push is unreachable for a new branch without its own upstream

- Finding ID: `R1 — first push cannot be reached for a new branch without a current-branch upstream`
- Review harnesses:
  - open_code_review [current_repository] (`open_code_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:open_code_review`) — generated the supported source finding.
  - Copilot: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash (provider default) [current_repository] (`copilot_review`, job `copilot-external-openrouter-deepseek-deepseek-v4-1-flash-80207ac38ad5:current_repository:copilot_review`) — corroborated the upstream-before-push ordering.
- Simple description: The GitHub PR path requires the current branch to already have an upstream before it reaches its push helper. A new branch therefore skips instead of performing the story-required first push and opening its PR.
- Example: A developer starts the GitHub review cycle on a new feature branch whose base branch tracks `origin/main`, but the feature branch has never been pushed. Looking up `@{u}` fails first, so the flow records `UPSTREAM_MISSING` and cannot create the external-review PR.
- Why accepted: Current Acceptance Criteria explicitly require automatic first push using the existing upstream remote. Current HEAD has the exact early-return seam and existing base-branch, Git-command, and push mechanisms needed for a narrow repair. The realistic failed PR path and its impact are material; the repair is limited to the configured base-branch remote and does not authorize arbitrary remotes, forks, fallback policy, or retry behavior. It is appropriate for the normal repair opportunity, not a final tasking decision.

#### 2. A warning-following authored wait can be discarded before it resumes

- Finding ID: `R3 — a warning followed by an authored persisted wait may never resume`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`) — generated and source-verified the static finding.
- Simple description: A supported GitHub skip records a terminal warning, while a later authored wait can still be persisted. When due, the wake guard can clear that valid wait instead of resuming the same flow execution.
- Example: The repository lacks the GitHub token, so PR opening produces the supported warning; the next authored wait is stored. Once its delay expires, the terminal-status guard can discard it before resume dispatch, leaving the flow stopped until an operator intervenes.
- Why accepted: Acceptance Criteria require persisted waits to resume automatically with the same execution identity and require the skip to remain a truthful warning. Current HEAD retains the existing persisted-context, guard, and resume-dispatch seam, and the existing integration test proves the warning-then-wait state is reachable. The missing due-wake runtime reproduction is preserved as a limitation, but the supported stuck-flow scenario is materially consequential and the limited repair is proportionate. It is appropriate for the normal repair opportunity, not a final tasking decision.

### Ignored for This Story

#### 3. Copied opt-in flow is absent from the main Compose catalog

- Finding ID or Review reference: `R2 — copied opt-in GitHub-review flow is absent from the main Compose flow catalog`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`) — generated the catalog observation.
- Simple description: The claim was that the copied opt-in flow under the repository's `flows/` directory could not be discovered by the main Compose stack.
- Example: The app-local flow directory is `/app/flows-sandbox`, but the current discovery and selected-repository loading paths also inspect an ingested repository's `flows/` directory; current integration coverage proves the copied variant is listed and runnable.
- Why ignored: The complete claim and its duplicate-catalog remedy were factually rejected during reconciliation before any survivor gate. It is preserved only to prevent resurrection as repair, task work, or review-loop continuation.

#### 4. Ownerless scheduled waits may be shown as orphaned

- Finding ID or Review reference: `R4 — healthy persisted/scheduled waits are reported as orphaned`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`) — generated and source-verified the static observation.
- Simple description: A running flow without active ownership can be reported as `orphaned`, even though an authored scheduled wait intentionally releases ownership while it remains persisted.
- Example: A flow stores an authored wait and its active owner is released. The lifecycle-status calculation can return `orphaned`, but retained evidence does not show a harmful client, recovery, or API consequence.
- Why ignored: The complete finding survived negative scope but was removed by positive authorization. ### Accepted

#### 1. Older paused cycle can overwrite a newer cycle's selector

- Finding ID: `R1 — older paused cycle can overwrite a newer cycle's selector`
- Review harnesses:
  - Codex review — Story 0000060 (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`, source job `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da`) — generated and verified the finding.
- Simple description: A paused GitHub review execution retains a pending-publication Boolean that later grants it permission to replace a selector owned by another execution. An older cycle can therefore make its feedback current after a newer cycle has fetched successfully.
- Example: Execution A opens a PR and waits. Execution B opens, fetches, and publishes review feedback for the same story; when A resumes, its retained flag allows it to overwrite B’s selector, so classification can read A’s older feedback instead.
- Why accepted: Current HEAD proves the pending flag, replacement path, and missing ordering control. The current story contract expressly requires fresh fetched state to remain active and authorizes the minimum private persisted state needed to preserve that ordering. The supported overlap can cause false clean completion or repair against the wrong cycle, and the existing scratch-path, context, lock, and writer seams can express a narrow normal repair without introducing public policy. It is not already resolved and is accepted only for the normal repair attempt, not final task creation.

### Accepted

#### 1. Reusing an open PR can send stale code through the review cycle

- Finding ID: `F1 — Reusing an open PR can send stale code through the review cycle`
- Review harnesses:
  - review_artifacts_main [current_repository] (`review_artifacts_main`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:review_artifacts_main`, source job `add5adb181d3d0428b0b8f60b21146c3f3409b9ffb37fc0a6c3bb679b2d8d399`, target `current_repository`) — generated F1 and its saturation, blind-spot, consolidated, and verification records corroborated it.
- Simple description: An existing PR is reused without checking whether its remote head still matches the local branch revision. The review cycle can therefore inspect older code while treating it as the current implementation.
- Example: A developer adds local commits after an existing PR was published, then starts the next review cycle. The flow reuses the old PR without pushing or comparing revisions, so reviewers comment on stale code and the newer local revision can receive a clean result without review.
- Why accepted: F1 is positively authorized by the current-branch and implementation-context contract, materially affects the core review outcome, and has a narrow existing lookup/push/re-lookup seam. It is retained only for normal-repair consideration; no repair, task, or stronger-attempt decision is made here, and no force-push, retry, alternate-remote, fork, or broad stale-PR policy is accepted.

#### 2. Reusing or recovering an open PR can accept the wrong base branch

- Finding ID: `F2 — Reusing or recovering an open PR can accept the wrong base branch`
- Review harnesses:

- Simple description: PR reuse and resume check the head branch but do not require the PR’s base branch to match the cycle’s selected base. The flow can review and classify feedback for the wrong merge target.
- Example: The same feature branch has a newer open PR to `release` while this cycle resolves `main` as its required base. Lookup or resume accepts the `release` PR, so feedback about that diff is treated as feedback for the `main` review cycle.
- Why accepted: F2 is positively authorized by the explicit trustworthy-base and same-context-on-resume contract, materially prevents wrong-target review routing, and can use existing base fields and failure paths. It is retained only for normal-repair consideration; no repair, task, or stronger-attempt decision is made here, and it does not authorize selecting another base or PR, a new retry policy, configuration, or broader recovery behavior.

### Accepted

#### 1. GitHub review-flow predicates resolved harness helpers from the worked repository

- Finding ID: `R-1`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`) — generated and source-corrobated the finding.
- Simple description: The copied GitHub-review flow used harness helper paths as implicit `if.condition` scripts. A normal worked repository resolved those paths beneath itself, so the flow failed before PR creation.
- Example: A user selects the opt-in flow for a repository without the harness `scripts/flow_control` directory; its first predicate cannot resolve the harness helper and the review cycle cannot open a PR.
- Why accepted: The materiality survivor was research-owned because of the historical root-ownership conflict. That bounded research invocation was the stronger opportunity and repaired the current implicit-if form in `bd8ff232f7872895f3325bec0f0d50af43009a0b`; it is resolved, not open task work.

#### 2. Persisted subflow waits could recover before their authored wake

- Finding ID: `R-2`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`) — generated and source-corrobated the finding.
- Simple description: A child with a valid persisted authored wait could be classified as orphaned and resumed before `resumeAt`.
- Example: A `subflowWave` child releases run ownership for a timed wait; parent polling treats it as orphaned and resumes it before the scheduled wake.
- Why accepted: The materiality survivor was distinct from the research false matches and was fixed by ordinary repair in `7c4759664698f9e44359ad0b37390f30a5b8ee7a`. The negative-scope removal of a new explicit paused lifecycle state remains binding.

### Ignored for This Story

- None. Partial/unavailable Copilot coverage, OpenCode's bounded no-findings result, and the one-target cross-repository no-work result remain coverage limits, not contradictory findings.

### Accepted

#### 1. Parent flow could remain stranded after a persisted child wait survived restart

- Finding ID: `P1`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`) — generated and source-corrobated the finding.
- Simple description: Startup scheduled the persisted child wait but left its active-child parent orphaned, so the parent could not consume the child's terminal result.
- Example: A server restarts while a child waits; the child wakes normally, but the parent stays non-terminal instead of completing the composed execution.
- Why accepted: Repeated research rejected historical false matches and returned this materiality survivor to ordinary repair. Normal repair committed `457e033a3de26ff5cde0f4ef7b9575355fc4fe2f`, so this finding is resolved and preserved as completed batch evidence.

#### 2. Parent stop did not cancel a persisted child wait

- Finding ID: `P2`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`) — generated and source-corrobated the finding.
- Simple description: Parent cancellation targeted a released child token and was not reapplied after the scheduled wake adopted a new token.
- Example: Stopping a parent during a child's 900-second review wait could leave the parent blocked until the wait naturally ended.
- Why accepted: Repeated research confirmed this as the earlier released-ownership stop gap and was the stronger opportunity. It fixed the parent entrypoint in `822e0d62a3f44d3921b3f455fa1a0c720c0270b4`; the completed record preserves the passing focused proof and incomplete broad-stress result.

### Accepted

#### 1. A nonfatal GitHub-review warning can permanently pause a later authored wait

- Finding ID: `P1 — A nonfatal GitHub-review warning can permanently pause a later authored wait`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (`codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`)
- Simple description: An ordinary authored wait scheduled after a supported GitHub-review warning treats the warning as terminal at wake time. It clears its scheduler entry before resuming, leaving the same flow execution paused.
- Example: A repository has no `CODEINFO_PR_TOKEN`, so the GitHub open step records the supported warning and the next authored wait is persisted. At the wait deadline, the wake guard clears that wait instead of dispatching `resumeFlowRun`, so an operator must intervene.
- Why accepted: Current HEAD still contains the exact existing wake-guard seam, and the integration test proves the supported warning-then-wait setup. ### Accepted

#### 1. Current-branch upstream fallback can select the base branch remote

- Finding ID: `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da:work/native-response.md:candidate-1:current_repository`

- Simple description: When the current feature branch has no upstream, the resolver adopts the base branch's upstream remote and pushes the feature branch through it. This can use a remote the current branch was never configured to track.
- Example: A new `feature/0000060-demo` branch has no `@{u}`, while `main@{u}` is `origin/main`. The resolver selects `origin` and the push seam can run `git push origin HEAD:feature/0000060-demo`, instead of taking the existing supported `UPSTREAM_MISSING` skip path.
- Why accepted: Current HEAD and the focused unit test prove the behavior. The current Description and Acceptance Criteria require automatic first push only through the current branch's existing upstream, and Out Of Scope forbids guessing alternate remotes. The existing resolver, `UPSTREAM_MISSING` outcome, and focused test provide a proportionate normal-repair seam; it is not duplicate or already resolved.

### Accepted

#### 1. Resume initialization can lose the selected GitHub-review context

- Finding ID: `F2` / `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da:work/native-response.md:P2:current_repository`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (flow `codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`, target `current_repository`, directory `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da`) — generated the finding; its native response, output, and verification corroborate the static observation.
  - review_artifacts_main [current_repository] (flow `review_artifacts_main`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:review_artifacts_main`, target `current_repository`, directory `add5adb181d3d0428b0b8f60b21146c3f3409b9ffb37fc0a6c3bb679b2d8d399`) — independently generated the later batch's equivalent P2 and corroborated the same first-persistence context-loss behavior before its committed repair.
- Simple description: The first persistence write of a resumed flow omits the existing GitHub-review context while rebuilding the saved flow state. An interruption in that window can lose the selected PR and scratch identity before normal runtime checkpoints restore it.
- Example: A flow paused for GitHub review resumes after a server restart with PR 42 selected. If the process stops after startup persistence but before the next checkpoint, the persisted state no longer contains that context; the next resume can select a different latest open PR instead of continuing PR 42's cycle.
- Why accepted: At the reviewed commit, the accepted contract requires the same execution and in-progress GitHub-review state after resume, while the initial persistence seam omits the context that the builder, restoration path, and normal checkpoint already expose. Preserving it needs no new policy and is materially worthwhile because the restart window can break the required execution ownership.
- Settlement status: This research-owned finding consumed its stronger opportunity without a commit because mandatory broad proof exposed an independent fresh-run completion-boundary failure. Batch `0000060-rw-20260921T014321Z-253d57f9` later committed the same narrow context-preservation repair at `ed7733cb8a6671af87f0483ec176adf0f4b49e45`; F2 is resolved and creates no open implementation task.

### Ignored for This Story

#### 2. Automatic stale-head feedback filtering and the absent-ID policy

- Finding ID or Review reference: `F1` / `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da:work/native-response.md:P1:current_repository` (present-ID mismatch core, plus the negative-gate removal of the absent-ID remedy)
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (flow `codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`, target `current_repository`, directory `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da`) — generated the underlying observation; the audited negative and positive gates preserved its source while removing its remedies from this story.
- Simple description: Feedback tied to an older PR head can reach classification because the filter does not automatically reject a present commit-ID mismatch. The proposed policy for feedback with no commit ID was narrowed away at negative scope, and automatic rejection of every present mismatch was not positively authorized.
- Example: A reviewer comment is attached to commit A and the branch later moves to B. The mismatch remains visible to classification, but the comment can still be relevant at B; treating it as stale before classification would impose a new rule. A missing ID likewise has no existing policy-free outcome.
- Why ignored: The absent-ID remedy is outside the authorized narrow scope because current HEAD exposes no such control and the story excludes solving every stale-PR edge case. The remaining present-ID rule is technically supported but not positively authorized: the plan makes feedback clean only after it is classified stale, not whenever its ID differs from the current head. It therefore did not reach materiality and cannot create repair, tasking, or review-loop continuation for this story.

### Accepted

#### 1. Initial resumed-run persistence can drop canonical GitHub review context

- Finding ID: `P2 — initial resumed-run persistence can drop canonical GitHub review context` (source job `target_reviews:current_repository:review_artifacts_main`, target `current_repository`)
- Review harnesses:
  - review_artifacts_main [current_repository] (flow `review_artifacts_main`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:review_artifacts_main`, target `current_repository`, directory `add5adb181d3d0428b0b8f60b21146c3f3409b9ffb37fc0a6c3bb679b2d8d399`) — generated the finding and corroborated it through evidence, saturation, blind-spot, consolidated output, and verification artifacts.
  - codex_review [current_repository] (flow `codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`, target `current_repository`, directory `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da`) — independently generated the earlier batch's equivalent F2 and supplied the historical attempted-repair evidence used during settlement.
- Simple description: The first persisted record for a resumed flow keeps `wait` but can omit a valid top-level GitHub review context. If the run stops before a later checkpoint, recovery can lose the selected PR and scratch authority needed to continue the same review cycle.
- Example: A resumed execution has its PR 206 context only at the top level. Starting it writes the running record without that context; if the server stops before the asynchronous flow checkpoints, the next resume cannot reliably recover PR 206 or its execution-scoped scratch state.
- Why accepted: The current reviewed commit proves the existing initial persistence seam omits the context while runtime precedence and later checkpoints preserve it. The Description and Acceptance Criteria require the same execution and in-progress GitHub-review cycle to survive a paused-wait resume. The narrow existing-parameter restoration is not excluded by any Out Of Scope restriction, is materially supported by a realistic restart window, and adds no new policy, schema, identity, retry, timeout, or PR-selection behavior.
- Settlement status: Commit `ed7733cb8a6671af87f0483ec176adf0f4b49e45`, recorded by Task 88, resolved this accepted finding with deterministic focused proof. The batch's repeated-routing attempt wrote only an unavailable record under a malformed lookalike batch identity, even though historical Task 44 and commit `869016a47f0a710b950217139ffa0864a398665b` provide finding-specific attempted-repair evidence. Settlement therefore does not represent the repeated stage as successful or the later normal-repair routing as clean; it preserves that procedural limitation while recognizing the actual committed repair. No open implementation task remains.

### Ignored for This Story

#### 1. Execution-scoped GitHub-review handoff leaf symlink bypasses containment

- Finding ID or Review reference: `R1` / `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da` / `current_repository`
- Review harnesses:
  - codex_review [current_repository] (flow `codex_review`, job `target_reviews:current_repository:codex_review`, target `current_repository`, directory `2335ad631923e8c9fed2b47b4b6f973e035c58c9381640a3ba7fe8f8210487da`) — generated R1; its verification corroborated the source-level behavior.
- Simple description: The handoff reader can follow an escaping symlink if the canonical execution-scoped leaf is replaced after publication. It could then make its yes/no decision from JSON outside the required review scratch location.
- Example: After the ordinary publisher writes the handoff, an independent process replaces that leaf with a symlink to external valid JSON. The path comparison succeeds through the same link and the decision reader could return `yes` from that external file.
- Why ignored: R1 is technically supported and positively authorized only for an existing resolved-scratch-root containment check. The materiality gate removed it because no supported flow replaces the controlled leaf with a symlink; the trigger depends on unproven external mutation after a temporary-file-and-rename publication. The broader blanket symlink-rejection remedy was also narrowed away because contained symlink targets remain supported. The available evidence does not demonstrate sufficient realistic reachability, impact, or value for changing completed Story 60 code.

#### 2. Ingest repository-root discovery honours ambient Git overrides

- Finding ID or Review reference: `R2` / `1c490b1e1d8854bdbc04a38cd48a284c1ace68316391a6312a81d022ac9e9ece` / `current_repository`
- Review harnesses:
  - Copilot: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash (provider default) [current_repository] (flow `copilot_review`, job `copilot-external-openrouter-deepseek-deepseek-v4-1-flash-80207ac38ad5:current_repository:copilot_review`, target `current_repository`, directory `1c490b1e1d8854bdbc04a38cd48a284c1ace68316391a6312a81d022ac9e9ece`) — generated R2; its verifier corroborated the source predicate.
- Simple description: Inherited Git environment overrides can make ingest root discovery select or fail against a different work tree. That can cause repository-wide ingestion to operate on the wrong repository.
- Example: A process with a foreign `GIT_WORK_TREE` invokes ingestion from the intended repository. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` can return the foreign root, which discovery then treats as the repository to enumerate.
- Why ignored: The completed negative scope gate removed the whole finding. Current-HEAD history assigns this behavior to an inherited Story 64 lifecycle merge, while Story 60 authorizes GitHub-review flow and persisted-state behavior—not generic ingest discovery or ambient-Git policy. Neither sanitizing Git environment/start-path containment nor restoring the old `.git` walk is authorized here; it remains a separate possible follow-up, not Story 60 work.
